findings.finding: The spec's checker rule, applied literally (any job whose if: reads needs.<job>.outputs must call always() and test that job's result), flags nine jobs across release.yaml and release-envoy-infra.yaml while the Done-when names three; rewriting only three turns the required lint job red, and three of the nine (the *_build jobs) are correct today and share the idiom of fifteen jobs in envoy-and-contracts.yaml.
findings.answer: Rule 6 is stated as two machine-checkable hazard clauses: 6a an if: that calls always() tests needs.<X>.result for every X whose outputs it reads; 6b an if: that calls no always() belongs to a job with no ancestor (through needs, any distance) that carries an if: of its own. Prototyped over the three workflows it flags exactly six jobs (legion_build, worker_image, legion_publish, worker_image_release_note, envoy_plugin_publish; infra publish), all rewritten in this PR; the *_build jobs pass. Recorded as spec departures 1 and 2.

findings.finding: The spec's trigger (reads needs.<job>.outputs) misses the result-only shape (if: needs.X.result == 'success' with no always()), which the same implicit success() skips — half of worker_image_release_note's own shape.
findings.answer: Clause 6b covers it (no always() + a skippable ancestor is flagged whatever the condition reads); the harness gets the red case `needs.pi_envoy_build.result == 'success'` and the sandbox probe a `control_result_only` arm.

findings.finding: always() vs !cancelled(), and whether the checker accepts success() as the status function.
findings.answer: always() is used (the spec's word; the file's precedent at release.yaml:226,462,793,986 and the listener's :364; cancel-in-progress: false means only a person cancels; publish steps are repeatable). Rule 6 accepts only always(); success() is treated as no status function (6b), pinned red in the harness and shown skipped in the probe's control_success arm. !cancelled() is named in the plan as the one-line alternative the architect may choose.

findings.finding: Done-when bullet 2 names a run in which envoy_plugin_build is skipped and says a workflow_dispatch is such a run; on a dispatch every *_build runs, so the criterion is unsatisfiable as written.
findings.answer: Restated (spec departure 3): in the proof run at least one job on legion_publish's ancestor path has conclusion skipped and legion_publish has conclusion success, read with gh run view --json jobs; what skips on a dispatch is a *_publish whose build printed skip=true, true for all three plugins today.

findings.finding: legion_build cutting a version on the post-merge dispatch is a precondition, not a given.
findings.answer: A4 names the precondition check (git log legion-v13.4.0..origin/main over legion's release paths; two commits today), the in-run line (`Bumping legion-v13.4.0 -> legion-v13.4.1`), the re-release case (a legion-v tag already at HEAD) and the fallback (wait for a qualifying push).

findings.finding: No acceptance covers the jobs whose conditions change but whose behaviour must not.
findings.answer: The plan carries a per-job semantics table, and A4 adds the regression check that every *_publish conclusion matches its build's skip output in the proof run; the infra publish condition is exercised by the release-envoy-infra.yaml run the merge itself starts (its on.push.paths includes the workflow file).

findings.finding: Where rule 6 runs inside the checker (the per-job loop visits only jobs with steps; worker_image has none), and what it does with a needs entry naming no job (the harness's green fixture has one).
findings.answer: Rule 6 is a pass of its own beside rules 4-5 over every job, steps or not; the header's Scope paragraph and the LEGION-748 solutions document's rule 5 are reworded; unknown needs names are ignored (GitHub refuses such a workflow at parse), pinned by the green fixture with a comment.

findings.finding: No semantics table: which runs change behaviour beyond the intended fix (legion_build/worker_image gaining needs.changes.result tightens a dispatch whose changes job failed; always() runs in a cancelled run).
findings.answer: The table is in the plan; the tightening is accepted with its reason (a failed changes is an infrastructure failure, not a release); the cancelled-run exposure is named as the one the three existing always() publish jobs already carry and goes into Not proven / risk.

findings.finding: Harness mechanics: mutate anchors adjacent to pi_envoy_build and cache-mode, the verbatim summary line, and omitted boundaries (bracket form, case, folded if:, non-string if:, two-needs one-result).
findings.answer: The fixture change places pi_envoy_build's if: after its permissions block so the three anchors stay intact; the summary line is unchanged; the case table lists each boundary with the clause and the token the message must name.

findings.finding: What can be proven before merge and the branch-dispatch hazard.
findings.answer: A3 is a sandbox probe on sjawhar/legion-smoke with a 13-job matrix (controls for the old shape, success(), result-only, two-needs; the always()-without-result hazard on a failed upstream); the plan forbids dispatching release.yaml from the branch with the reason (the *_build jobs publish from any ref) and lists what only the post-merge run proves.

findings.finding: Acceptance bullet 3 names no expected output and bullet 2's attestation check names no command.
findings.answer: A5 requires equality with the two lines the run's own Smoke test step logged; A4 names gh release view/download, sha256sum -c, and the gh attestation verify invocation with the signer and source digest pinned.

findings.finding: The Problem names legion-v13.4.0's release body still lacking a ## Worker image section; the Done-when does not repair it.
findings.answer: Out of scope in the plan with the reason (the note job edits only its own run's tag; nothing reads 13.4.0's body once 13.4.1 exists); named to the architect as its decision.

findings.finding: Documentation that goes stale: AGENTS.md:127, the checker header, the test header, the LEGION-748 solutions document's rule 5.
findings.answer: All four are file-level steps of the plan with their wording; docs/kubernetes.md needs no change.

findings.finding: Live-state claims the analyst could not verify (run job results, tags, no run since, the pre-#1969 guard).
findings.answer: Verified by the planner with gh (run 38822866387's job list, tags ending at legion-v13.4.0 → 74246501, no later release.yaml run on main) and carried into A4 as commands the implementer re-runs; the pre-#1969 history claim is marked as not re-verified and not relied on.

specDepartures.spec: check-release-credentials.sh fails when a release-workflow job reads needs.<job>.outputs in its if: without always() and that job's result.
specDepartures.plan: Rule 6 has two clauses: (6a) an if: that calls always() tests needs.<X>.result for every X whose outputs it reads; (6b) an if: that calls no always() (absent, or success() or any other function) belongs to a job with no ancestor through needs, at any distance, that carries an if: of its own. Job-level if: only, every job of the three workflows, steps or not.
specDepartures.evidence: The literal rule flags nine jobs including envoy_plugin_build, pi_envoy_build and pi_legion_build (if: needs.changes.outputs.<x> == 'true' || workflow_dispatch), correct today because changes carries no if:, and the idiom of fifteen jobs in envoy-and-contracts.yaml; and it passes if: needs.legion_build.result == 'success' with no always(), which the same implicit success() skips (worker_image_release_note at release.yaml:487 is half that shape and was skipped in run 38791202705).

outcome.scope: Done-when bullet 1's checker clause: the checker fails a needs.<job>.outputs read without always() when the job has a skippable ancestor, and always() without needs.<job>.result in every case; it does not fail pi_envoy_build's condition.

specDepartures.spec: release.yaml's legion_publish, worker_image_release_note and envoy_plugin_publish conditions carry always() and test the predecessor's result.
specDepartures.plan: Six conditions change: those three, plus legion_build and worker_image (add needs.changes.result == 'success'; they call always() and read needs.changes.outputs) and release-envoy-infra.yaml's publish (always() && needs.build.result == 'success' && needs.build.outputs.skip != 'true'; build carries if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main').
specDepartures.evidence: Rule 6 prototyped over the three workflows in the pod flags exactly these six; CI's required lint job runs the checker on the repository (pr-and-main.yaml:66), so every flagged condition must change in the same pull request. Behaviour change beyond the fix: a workflow_dispatch whose changes job failed no longer builds legion or the sha- image.

outcome.scope: Six job conditions across release.yaml and release-envoy-infra.yaml, not three.

specDepartures.spec: On main, a run of release.yaml in which envoy_plugin_build is skipped and legion_build cuts a version runs legion_publish to success; a workflow_dispatch of release.yaml on main after the merge is such a run.
specDepartures.plan: The proof run is one in which at least one job on legion_publish's ancestor path has conclusion skipped and legion_publish has conclusion success (gh run view <id> --json jobs); a workflow_dispatch gives that when a plugin has nothing new since its tag (its *_publish skips), which holds today for all three.
specDepartures.evidence: On a dispatch every *_build runs on its github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' clause (release.yaml:526, 705, 892) and the changes job's filter steps are skipped (:106, :132), so envoy_plugin_build is never skipped on a dispatch; what skips is a *_publish whose build printed skip=true (:599, :794, :987).

outcome.acceptance: Done-when bullet 2 names 'a job upstream of legion_publish is skipped' rather than 'envoy_plugin_build is skipped'.
